Elena (People Ops): FYI PioneerTrust just emailed: they're ending support for small-employer plans and want us to pick a successor trustee by 2024-04-15. They've provided a transfer CSV and a signed-consent requirement.
Tom (Payroll): I saw it. Key ops question: how do we handle deferrals that hit payroll between now and 4/15? We need a cutoff mapping or a remap instruction to send to payroll vendor.
Anika (Benefits): Vendor packet says loans can be rolled to successor trustee only if trustee accepts loan transfers; otherwise outstanding balances trigger taxable distributions. They also flagged Roth-in-plan conversions as "non-transferable" in their doc.
Elena (People Ops): That's a new wrinkle. If Roth conversions can't transfer, folks might see weird balances. We need an FAQ for employees about checking Roth/after-tax accounts.
Sam (Legal): I'll review the PioneerTrust termination clause and notification timelines. Also confirm whether vendor followed the contract notice window; if not, we may have leverage to delay effective processing.
Tom (Payroll): Proposed short ops plan: 1) Freeze voluntary deferral edits for Pioneer plan until mapping confirmed. 2) Generate participant export with columns `employee_id,last_deferral,catchup_flag,loan_balance,account_type`. 3) Flag pay runs that would process after 4/15 for manual remap.
Anika (Benefits): I'll request the successor trustee intake spec and ask if they accept e-sign and bulk transfers. If they accept loans, include loan account IDs in the CSV.
PrefsBot: Note created: vendor-exit-2312345678; assigned to @Anika @Tom @Elena.
Elena (People Ops): Communication idea: urgent short note first: "PioneerTrust transition planning — do not change your deferral elections for the Pioneer plan until we confirm mapping." Follow with a detailed FAQ covering loans, Roth, international tax, and required signed consent.
Tom (Payroll): I'll post a redacted sample from the export tonight so Benefits/Legal can see edge cases. Example rows: `employee_id,name,last_deferral,loan_balance`
```
10001,REDACTED,600,0
10045,REDACTED,200,3500
10100,REDACTED,650,0
```
Anika (Benefits): Successor trustee (BrightRiver) replied: accepts trustee-to-trustee loan rollovers and e-sign PDFs. They asked for `ssn,last4,dob,account_type,transfer_amount` and a signed participant consent per person. Also requested clarification on Roth holdings — they can accept Roth balances but not in-plan conversions mid-transfer.
Sam (Legal): For employees age 55+ doing catch-up, confirm whether catch-up deferrals are treated separately in the mapping. Also check international tax implications for UK/Canada-based employees.
Elena (People Ops): Decision point: will Redwood collect signatures centrally or require individuals to sign? Central collection speeds batch transfers but requires consent text and an upload workflow. Thoughts?
Anika (Benefits): Central collection preferred. BrightRiver accepts e-sign and we can host a short upload page. I'll coordinate a CSV + consent PDF bundle per participant.
Tom (Payroll): If we central collect, payroll needs the final mapping CSV by noon two business days before the pay date for off-cycle remaps. Keep that deadline in mind.
Sam (Legal): I'll prepare the consent blurb and retention policy. Also drafting an FAQ entry about Roth conversion edge cases.
Elena (People Ops): OK team: Anika confirm intake spec + e-sign by 3pm; Tom post export by 2pm; Sam consent text by 4pm. I'll draft the urgent note for 5pm send. Keeping this thread as the master log. :eyes:
